summary:
THE LAST LIGHT is an interactive space mission design and simulation game developed by Team N3bul@N00dl3s for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Inspired by the challenge of designing and operating space missions, ASTRA allows players to plan a mission by selecting destinations, spacecraft, scientific instruments, and launch vehicles while balancing constraints such as fuel, budget, mass, and power. Players then simulate their missions, respond to unexpected flight conditions, manage spacecraft communication through ground stations, and track scientific objectives.

The project transforms complex space mission concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience. By introducing players to the engineering trade-offs, resource management, and communication challenges involved in space exploration, ASTRA encourages curiosity about space science and mission design. It demonstrates how interactive technology can make the principles of real-world space exploration more accessible, understandable, and enjoyable.
details:
PROJECT ASTRA

What does it do and how does it work?

Users begin by designing their own space mission, selecting a destination, mission objectives, spacecraft, scientific instruments, and launch vehicle. They must balance important engineering constraints, including budget, fuel, spacecraft mass, power, and overall spacecraft health.

Once the mission is designed, users can launch the simulation and manage the spacecraft as the mission progresses. They encounter changing flight conditions and unexpected challenges that require decisions and adjustments. The simulation also introduces communication delays, ground-station contact windows, and scientific data transmission, demonstrating how spacecraft communicate with Earth. Users can monitor mission objectives, view a flight map, evaluate mission outcomes, and generate a downloadable PDF mission report.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRA makes complex space mission concepts more accessible through interactive learning and experimentation. Instead of simply reading about space exploration, users can experience the decisions and trade-offs involved in mission planning. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, scientific curiosity and an understanding of aerospace engineering concepts.

Our goal is to inspire students and aspiring space enthusiasts to explore STEM fields while developing a greater appreciation of the complexity of space exploration.

Tools and Technologies Used

The project was developed using:

React for the interactive user interface.

JavaScript and TypeScript for application logic and functionality.

HTML5 and CSS3 for structure and styling.

Vite for development and production builds.

Amazon S3 website hosting for deployment and public access.

PDF generation functionality for downloadable mission reports.

Creativity and Design Considerations

ASTRA combines educational content with game-based mission simulation. Its distinctive approach is to turn mission planning into a series of meaningful decisions where every choice can influence the mission outcome. We considered usability, realistic engineering trade-offs, resource limitations, communication delays, scientific objectives, and mission progression when developing the experience.

By bringing these elements together in an accessible interactive environment, PROJECT ASTRA aims to make the fascinating challenges of space exploration engaging and understandable for a wider audience.
